rationale: C23 supplies an almost complete person-substitution template for the child: the same retirement-trigger recital, public-interest finding, statutory authority, and operative exemption for an indefinite period. C24 is comparably close, while C03 has virtually identical recitals but its supplied text omits the operative provision.

shared_material.child_excerpt: will, during the month of November 1952, become subject to compulsory retirement for age under the provisions of the Civil Service Retirement Act of May 29, 1930, as amended, unless exempted therefrom by Executive order
shared_material.parent_excerpt: will, during the month of March 1952, become subject to compulsory retirement for age under the provisions of the Civil Service Retirement Act of May 29, 1930, as amended unless exempted therefrom by Executive order
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive retirement-trigger recital reproduced with only the person and month changed.

shared_material.child_excerpt: WHEREAS, in my judgment, the public interest requires that the said person be exempted from such compulsory retirement as provided below
shared_material.parent_excerpt: WHEREAS, in my judgment, the public interest requires that the said person be exempted from such compulsory retirement as provided below

shared_material.child_excerpt: by virtue of the authorized vested in me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 404 (5 U.S.C. 715a), I hereby exempt the said Theodore Marks from compulsory retirement for age for an indefinite period of time
